prompt:
Image 1 is a style reference only: match its painting style, brushwork, lighting, rim light, framing, background and proportions. The person, the face, the headgear and every ornament must be different from Image 1 and must follow the description below exactly; do not copy the man, the helm, the horns or the trim from Image 1.
Image 2 is a painted portrait of a Thornwood leader from the same set, a reference for the nation's materials only (bark plate, leaf cloth, weathered bark-brown skin): do not paint that person, and do not give the soldier a leader's ornaments, crown, antlers or rich trim.

Head-and-shoulders portrait bust of one soldier, three-quarter view, the face turned toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the top of the head or headgear about 9% from the top edge, the eyes about 39% from the top, the chin about 62% from the top, the image cut at mid-chest, with dark empty space above and around the head. One figure only. Nothing behind the head or the shoulders: no shield, no sword hilt, no spear, no hands, no text, no border, no frame, no signature, no logo.
Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the back of the head or headgear, the hair and the shoulders that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible brushwork, moderate detail, a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the headgear and the light face against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 48 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy, except the side's deep pine green cloth (#1F6A50), which shows clearly on the shoulders (the leaf mantle), the tabard and the helm's leaf crest, so the card reads as that side at a glance. Nothing in the image glows.

Subject: A fighter of the Thornwood, forest clans who live among ancient trees: weathered bark-brown skin, bark-and-leaf clothing and armor in moss green and bark brown.
A Warden: armor of layered bark plates under a deep pine-green tabard that covers the chest and the back to mid-thigh, a rounded helm of overlapping bark plates (not a classical crested metal helmet) with a low crest of stiff deep pine-green leaves running front to back, the face open, a deep pine-green mantle of overlapping cloth leaves over the shoulders and upper back, a round shield of bark-covered wood whose face is painted deep pine green with a pale blossom sigil and a bark-brown rim, a straight leaf-bladed sword, bark-brown weathered skin.
Person: a common soldier of the line, not a leader; an ordinary weathered face of the nation above.
note: the pilot's Warden bust, kept by the owner ("Card bust: Keep"); made before the Warden sheet existed
